compiled_state.title: [fix-bug/cluster-investigation]: umbrella split-out propagates title-only attribution into child tickets -> phantom-symptom investigations consume ADVANCED-tier budget
compiled_state.author: Test
compiled_state.description:
## Background

Closure of bug 0ac3-dab8-abfd-4359 ("[tests/scripts/test-write-cycle-ledger.sh]: intermittent failures") revealed a process-level defect in how umbrella tickets get split into child tickets during cluster-investigation triage.

## Symptom

A ticket can be split out of an umbrella inheriting an "intermittent failure" symptom-claim that has **no captured CI evidence** anywhere — yet still consume ADVANCED-tier investigator budget (two opus investigators, one full hour) before the absence-of-evidence is detected.

## Concrete example (0ac3-dab8-abfd-4359 → 53f9-a218-8799-49be)

1. Umbrella 53f9 was filed 2026-05-17 citing same-commit-run-A-vs-B evidence for test-merge-to-main*.sh (4 specific assertion failures, 2 CI run links).
2. The umbrella's **TITLE** mentions test-write-cycle-ledger.sh — but the umbrella's **Actual Behavior** section enumerates only test-merge-to-main*.sh failures. No same-commit-A-vs-B evidence for test-write-cycle-ledger.sh is cited anywhere in the umbrella.
3. The cluster-investigation comment classified the umbrella as bundling 4 sub-tracks; Track B = "test-write-cycle-ledger.sh intermittent failures → DISPROVED as state-file race; separate investigation needed." The DISPROVED→separate-needed pattern carried the attribution forward without ever requiring an evidence link.
4. BASIC tier then offered a hypothesis ("most likely the concurrent-write test ... non-atomic assertion window") for the inherited (un-evidenced) symptom.
5. On user direction, the umbrella was split into 4 child tickets, one per track. Track B became 0ac3-dab8-abfd-4359 — inheriting the symptom-claim verbatim into the new ticket's description ("fails intermittently in CI. Same commit, same code — pass on one run, fail on the next.") despite zero captured CI evidence of that pattern for THIS test file.
6. ADVANCED-tier investigation (two opus investigators, code-tracer + historical) ran for ~58 minutes total and converged with HIGH confidence on: no defect exists; B3 lock correctly serializes concurrent writers; A2's race is benign; **and** no CI evidence of a same-commit-A-vs-B failure for test-write-cycle-ledger.sh exists in git history or in the umbrella's cited runs.

## Root cause (process)

Cluster-investigation and umbrella-split-out logic accepts attribution-by-title as sufficient grounds to propagate a symptom-claim into a child ticket. There is no evidence-link requirement on the propagation step. The pattern "DISPROVED as X; separate investigation needed" reinforces this — it carries the symptom-claim forward as established fact while simultaneously disproving the first explanatory hypothesis, locking in a phantom-symptom inheritance.

## Proposed fix

Before splitting an umbrella into a child ticket, require **at minimum one of**:
1. A specific CI run URL + failing test/assertion name observed in that run for the child's affected file, OR
2. An explicit `attribution_basis: speculative` flag in the child ticket header, with the BASIC-tier scoring rubric routing speculative-attribution tickets to a separate, lighter triage path (e.g., manual confirmation before any investigation budget is spent) instead of the standard tier-based investigation routing.

## Affected files

- plugins/dso/skills/fix-bug/SKILL.md (Cluster Investigation Mode logic)
- plugins/dso/skills/fix-bug/prompts/cluster-mode-protocol.md (or equivalent — split-out instructions)
- Possibly: plugins/dso/skills/create-bug/SKILL.md (require evidence link before creating a bug whose source is "split from umbrella X")

## Detected_by

User reflection on the 0ac3 closure question "if no defect exists, what caused the symptom reported in the bug?" — the answer "there was no documented symptom" surfaced the process-level pattern.
